quizName: DMV Practice Test #9 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, you should:

options.text: Speed up.
Make sudden moves.
Move to the edge of the road.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, slow down, avoid sudden moves, stay away from the road edge, and ride in the tire tracks left by other cars.

questions.question: When someone follows you too closely, you should:

options.text: Speed up.
Not worry about them and just focus on the road in front of you.
Change lanes and let them pass.
Ride on the shoulder and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Change lanes and let a tailgater pass you. Speeding up will only make them follow closer at a higher speed, which is more dangerous. Never ride on the shoulder because drivers won't expect you there and may suddenly leave the road.

questions.question: Most motorcycle crashes happen:

options.text: On short trips.
On long trips.
After at least an hour of riding.
After more than 8 hours of riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: On short trips.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on trips shorter than five miles, just a few minutes after the rider starts out.

questions.question: You will ______ hear a tire going flat.

options.text: Always
Usually
Frequently
Seldom

questions.correctAnswerText: Seldom
questions.explanation: You will seldom hear a tire go flat on a motorcycle. Instead, you will notice a sudden change in how the motorcycle handles.

questions.question: How can a motorcycle operator discourage lane sharing by other drivers?

options.text: By giving dirty looks to other drivers
By riding in the center portion of the lane
By riding in the left portion of the lane
By riding in a zigzag pattern

questions.correctAnswerText: By riding in the center portion of the lane
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane. This leaves less space on each side of your motorcycle and makes it harder for other drivers to try to share the lane with you.

questions.question: Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS) are designed to:

options.text: Prevent skidding and wheel lock-up.
Prevent brakes from activating if the roadway is dry.
Apply brakes automatically.
Warn you when your brake pad needs replacing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevent skidding and wheel lock-up.
questions.explanation: ABS prevents skidding and wheel lock-up during hard braking. When sensors detect that a wheel is about to lock, the system releases and reapplies brake pressure to keep the wheels spinning and maintain maximum braking power.

questions.question: When being passed, all of the following are potential hazards, except:

options.text: Extended mirrors.
Objects being thrown from other vehicles.
Blasts of wind.
Headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Headlights.
questions.explanation: When being passed, watch out for the vehicle's mirrors hitting you, wind gusts from the passing vehicle, and objects thrown from the vehicle. Headlights are not a hazard when being passed.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, it is best to:

options.text: Downshift.
Accelerate.
Grip the handlebars firmly and close the throttle gradually.
Gradually apply your brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Grip the handlebars firmly and close the throttle gradually.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up, as this will make the wobble worse. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly and slowly reduce speed by closing the throttle. Shift your weight forward and down. Pull off the road as soon as you can. Do not apply the brakes, as this may worsen the wobble.

questions.question: Passengers should:

options.text: Lean as the operator leans.
Hold onto their seat.
Sit as far back on the bike as possible.
Never hold onto the operator.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean as the operator leans.
questions.explanation: Passengers should sit directly behind the operator and lean with them through turns. They should sit as close to the operator as possible without crowding them and hold onto the operator's waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: Passengers should:

options.text: Lean with the operator.
Never come into contact with the operator.
Sit as far back on their seat as possible.
Hold onto their seat.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean with the operator.
questions.explanation: Before carrying a passenger, teach them to lean with you through turns and curves. They should hold onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: When stopped at an intersection, use your mirrors to:

options.text: See if parked cars are entering traffic.
Watch for vehicles changing lanes.
Check for vehicles behind you that may not be slowing down.
See if someone is turning behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for vehicles behind you that may not be slowing down.
questions.explanation: Use your mirrors to watch for cars approaching from behind. Drivers may not see you in time to stop.

questions.question: Drivers on an entrance ramp may not see you on the highway. What should you do?

options.text: Stay in your lane. It is not your responsibility to be seen.
Change to a lane away from the entrance ramp if you can.
Move to the shoulder.
Weave within your lane to be more visible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change to a lane away from the entrance ramp if you can.
questions.explanation: Give merging vehicles plenty of space. Change lanes away from the entrance ramp if it is safe. If you cannot change lanes, slow down to make room.

questions.question: Motorcyclists riding in a group should not ride in pairs because:

options.text: A merging driver may not see both riders.
Helmet reflections may make it hard for riders to see.
Riders do not have enough space to avoid hazards.
It is too hard for left-side riders to exit a highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riders do not have enough space to avoid hazards.
questions.explanation: Group riders should never ride in pairs. Neither rider will have enough room to move and avoid hazards.

questions.question: Before riding, your pre-ride check should include everything except:

options.text: Check the tires.
Check the taillight.
Check the headlight.
Check the paint.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check the paint.
questions.explanation: Check your tires, oil, fluids, lights, signals, clutch, throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn before every ride.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT affect blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?

options.text: The amount of alcohol consumed
How fast a person drinks
Body weight
Height

questions.correctAnswerText: Height
questions.explanation: BAC is affected by how much alcohol someone drinks, how fast they drink it, and their body weight.

questions.question: When entering a curve, a group should ride in:

options.text: Single-file formation.
Staggered formation.
Pairs.
On the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Single-file formation.
questions.explanation: Use single-file formation when turning, taking curves, or entering or exiting a highway. Staggered formation is usually best for other situations.

questions.question: A driver making eye contact with you:

options.text: Means they see you.
Will never happen.
Does not guarantee they will yield to you.
Guarantees they will yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not guarantee they will yield to you.
questions.explanation: Never assume eye contact means a driver will yield. Drivers often look directly at motorcyclists but do not consciously see them.

questions.question: Most crashes happen during the day. To reduce your crash risk, you should:

options.text: Wear dark-colored clothing.
Wear bright-colored clothing.
Not ride during the day.
Look for safer routes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear bright-colored clothing.
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors to be as visible as possible when riding, even during the day.

questions.question: If you shift into a lower gear while going too fast, the:

options.text: Motorcycle could jerk and the rear tire could skid.
Motorcycle could accelerate too quickly.
Front tire will likely skid.
Engine will make a loud noise.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycle could jerk and the rear tire could skid.
questions.explanation: If you shift into a lower gear while going too fast, the motorcycle will jerk and the rear wheel may skid.

questions.question: Riding between two vehicles moving in the same direction:

options.text: Is illegal.
Is okay if traffic is heavy.
Is okay during the day to prevent traffic jams.
Is okay if the motorcyclist is comfortable.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is illegal.
questions.explanation: In Oregon, motorcycles and mopeds cannot pass between two moving vehicles on a multilane highway or one-way street.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should riders do?

options.text: Use only their mirrors to check for other vehicles.
Turn their head to look for traffic behind them.
Ignore other traffic.
Brake hard so vehicles in their blind spot can pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn their head to look for traffic behind them.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots. Always turn your head to check for traffic before changing lanes.

questions.question: After mounting your motorcycle, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Make sure the mirrors are clean.
Make sure the horn works.
Close the fuel supply valve.
Make sure the clutch works smoothly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Close the fuel supply valve.
questions.explanation: After mounting your motorcycle, check that the clutch, throttle, horn, and brakes work properly. Clean and adjust the mirrors. Make sure the fuel supply valve is open, not closed.

questions.question: To see better when you prepare to pass a vehicle on its left, where should you ride?

options.text: In the left portion of your lane.
In the right portion of your lane.
In the center portion of your lane.
Stand up on your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the left portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane when preparing to pass. This increases what you can see and makes oncoming traffic see you better.

questions.question: When passing parked cars on your right with no oncoming traffic, where should you stay?

options.text: Toward the right side of your lane.
Toward the left side of your lane.
Look to your left frequently.
Use your rearview mirrors more often.

questions.correctAnswerText: Toward the left side of your lane.
questions.explanation: Stay on the side of your lane away from the parked cars. This protects you from open car doors and people stepping out between cars.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while riding and you need to stop, what should you do?

options.text: Relax your grip on the handlebars.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake gently on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
Use both brakes and stop quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake gently on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: If a tire fails, hold the handlebars firmly and slow down by easing off the throttle. If you must brake, gently apply the brake of the good tire. Move toward the side of the road as you slow down, squeeze the clutch, and stop.
